input_withheld_tax_nl: NL wage tax withheld by employer (€)
input_withheld_tax_nl_hint: From your annual statement (jaaropgave). Leave 0 to skip eindafrekening.
input_sick_days_hint: Days of sick leave during the year. NL and BE calculate the sourcing ratio differently for sick days.
summary_copy_error: Copy failed. Please allow clipboard access in your browser.
be_only_residents: Belgian tax only applies to residents of Belgium.
be_no_home_working: No days worked outside the Netherlands → no Belgian income tax due on salary.
be_warning_text: This is a simplified estimate. Your final return may differ due to spouse income splitting, special social security contributions, regional taxes and other personal deductions. Consult a tax advisor for your final tax return.
years_description: This comparison uses the exact same input values (salary, workdays, family status), only the selected tax year changes.
input_workdays_total_zero_warning: Enter at least one workday to calculate a realistic net/day amount.
input_workdays_total_high_warning: This seems high; please double-check if all day counts are correct.
wfh_description: Sweeps the NL ↔ BE day split while keeping total workdays fixed. Hover to inspect each scenario.
wfh_x_label: Days worked from home in 🇧🇪 BE (%)
wfh_qualifying_taxpayer_note: ≤10% BE (≥90% NL): you qualify as a 'kwalificerend buitenlands belastingplichtige'. Benefits: hypotheekrenteaftrek (mortgage interest deduction), aftrek ziektekosten (medical expenses), and heffingskorting niet-werkende partner (non-working partner credit). Requires an inkomensverklaring validated by Belgian tax authorities and sent to the Dutch Belastingdienst.
wfh_threshold_25_hint: Above this: Belgian income tax applies
wfh_hover_hint: Hover the chart to explore scenarios
summary_sourcing_nl_formula: NL method: (NL + sick days) ÷ (NL + BE + other + sick days) — sick days count as NL workdays
summary_sourcing_be_formula: BE method: NL days ÷ (NL + BE + other days) — sick days excluded from both numerator and denominator
summary_sourcing_overlap_note: ⚠️ With sick days and Belgian workdays recorded, the NL and BE sourcing fractions can sum to more than 100%: NL counts sick days as NL-sourced workdays, while BE excludes them entirely — making the BE fraction slightly larger than it would be otherwise. The overlap equals sick days × BE days ÷ [(NL + BE + sick) × (NL + BE)], which may result in a small portion of sick-day income being taxed by both countries (double taxation).
wfh_threshold_49_hint: Above this: Dutch social security no longer applies. Request kaderakkoord at SVB to stay covered (applies up to 49%).
wfh_kaderakkoord_note: Working 25–49% of your days from Belgium (telework): Dutch social security remains applicable if you apply for the kaderakkoord at SVB (requires an A1 document). Above 49%, Belgian social security applies.
input_workdays_nl_hint: Include: office days, training days, offsites, and business travel days. Exclude: vacation, ADV/compensation days, national holidays, and sick leave (enter sick days separately below). Overtime and commuting do not count.
input_workdays_typical: Tip: start from 260 days (52 × 5), then subtract vacation days, ADV/compensation days, and public holidays that fall on weekdays.
input_social_security_kaderakkoord: Kaderakkoord zone (25–49% BE days): Dutch social security remains applicable if you hold an A1 certificate. Request this jointly with your employer at SVB.
input_social_security_above_50: Above 49% BE days: Belgian social security would apply. Review your working arrangement.

ref_ss_tax_vs_ss_body: For social security there is a framework agreement that neutralises remote work (up to 49%). For tax there is no comparable rule. Every day working from home in Belgium is a day on which Belgium levies tax.
ref_ss_footer: Based on ACV Border Workers Checklist 2026 & Information Session 24 March 2026 (Pelt). No rights can be derived. Consult ACV Border Workers or a tax specialist for your personal situation.

ref_pension_term_confusion_body: "Pension" in the Netherlands = supplementary to AOW (2nd pillar). "Pension" in Belgium = the statutory pension. Don't confuse this when talking to HR or pension funds.
